To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We develop a general approach to robust change point detection based on transformations that are bounded from below and above.

the proposed change point tests are robust and powerful in the presence of heavy tailed data and outliers, and that they are able to detect changes in marginal variance of ARCH time series as well as changes in the dependence structure.

robust change point tests are more powerful than classical moment based change point procedures in case of non-Gaussian data and that the proposed robust change point tests perform well in case of ARCH processes and multivariate heavy tailed time series.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems: 1. Robust change point tests based bounded transformations.
the following questions: (1) How can one detect structural breaks in the mean, variance, or dependence of heavy tailed time series?
the following topics: 1. Robust change point tests for heavy tailed time series. 2. Robust change detection in multivariate time series with application to financial data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in detecting changes in marginal variances of ARCH processes and in detecting changes in dependence of multivariate heavy tailed processes.
the new class of robust tests for change points is a very powerful and flexible tool for the analysis of heavy tailed time series.
the proposed approach is very flexible, powerful and robust in a wide range of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new approach can be applied in a wide range of applications and is very powerful in case the data generating process is heavy tailed and/or contains outliers.
we provide a very flexible and powerful approach for detecting changes in the dependence structure or marginal distribution of heavy tailed time series.
the proposed approach allows to detect changes in the mean and scale of heavy tailed time series, which is not possible with classical moment based change point methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
robust change point detection is feasible and can be done in a very flexible way.
bounded transformations of the observations can be very useful to improve the performance of existing change point tests in heavy tailed time series.
the cusum test is very powerful and can be easily adapted to detect a wide range of changes in time series data.
